Source contracts: src/gateway_macos

src/gateway_macos/init.py

Python · Tier A

Keep the macOS Gateway package namespace stable.

Responsibilities

  • version re-exports the shared Gateway core version without inventing a platform-specific number.

Boundaries

  • Application composition and target execution are owned by app.py and gateway_core, not package import.

Lifecycle

  • Package initialization precedes platform app/config imports.

State

  • No package-owned durable state or process lifecycle is created here.

Security

  • Importing this namespace does not grant access to Gateway operations.

Collaborators

  • gateway_core/init.py owns the shared version; the platform app.py binds service composition.

Public surface

  • version re-exports the shared Gateway core version without inventing a platform-specific number.

@see src/gateway_core/init.py

@see src/gateway_macos/app.py

src/gateway_macos/app.py

Python · Tier A

Expose the macOS platform Gateway through the shared application factory.

Responsibilities

  • Bind platform settings to gateway_core.app.create_app and expose its ASGI application.

Boundaries

  • Routes, credentials, execution and job/terminal semantics belong to shared gateway_core; this wrapper does not duplicate them.

Lifecycle

  • First ASGI use creates the default app; explicit create_app(settings) allows isolated composition with supplied settings.

State

  • The exported app owns service state constructed by the shared factory. This wrapper adds no independent durable store or worker.

Security

  • Platform settings select the target environment; shared core authentication and execution checks remain authoritative.

Collaborators

  • gateway_macos/config.py selects platform identity and defaults; gateway_core/app.py registers transport/service endpoints.

Public surface

  • app is the launcher ASGI target; create_app returns a separately configured FastAPI instance. Retain platform import paths for compatibility.

@see src/gateway_macos/config.py

@see src/gateway_core/app.py

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
create_app 40 Create the shared Gateway API using explicit settings or cached macOS defaults. Service/route semantics remain owned by gateway_core rather than this platform wrapper.

src/gateway_macos/config.py

Python · Tier A

Select macOS node identity and POSIX shell defaults for Gateway composition.

Responsibilities

  • Prefer GATEWAY_NODE_NAME, then a bounded scutil LocalHostName lookup, then platform hostname. LLM runtime is disabled by default.

Boundaries

  • Shared Settings validation and service behavior remain in gateway_core.config; defaults do not confer execution authorization.

Lifecycle

  • The platform app calls get_settings at composition; operators can instead supply a Settings instance to the app factory.

State

  • get_settings caches one validated settings object per process. Restart or clear the cache to adopt changed environment input.

Security

  • Read named GATEWAY_* overrides and platform identity; do not expose credential values as presentation metadata.

Collaborators

  • gateway_core/config.py validates the shared schema; agent_runtime/branding.py supplies the public display title.

Public surface

  • Settings and get_settings retain the platform import contract; node naming affects identity and must not be casually renamed.

@see src/gateway_core/config.py

@see src/gateway_macos/app.py

@see src/agent_runtime/branding.py

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
get_settings 62 Construct and cache one macOS settings snapshot for this process. Environment changes require explicit cache reset or process restart.

src/gateway_macos/install.sh

Shell · Tier B

Install the macOS Gateway environment and verify canonical dependencies.

Usage

Run on each macOS Gateway host after updating its checkout.

Inputs

PYTHON_BIN selects Python 3.11+; platform package-discovery and skip controls apply where supported.

Side effects

Creates or repairs the platform .venv, updates packaging tools and calls scripts/update_gateway_runtime.py; package downloads modify that environment.

Cleanup

Exits on setup failure; no Gateway service is started or restarted. Rerun after resolving dependency errors.

@see scripts/update_gateway_runtime.py

@see src/gateway_macos/README.md

src/gateway_macos/reset-pairing.sh

Shell · Tier B

Reset macOS controller pairing using the installed Gateway interpreter.

Usage

Stop the Gateway before changing pairing; run as its service account and retain its TLS identity.

Inputs

Arguments pass to gateway_core.pairing reset-pairing; use the same GATEWAY_TLS_STATE_DIR as startup.

Side effects

Changes persisted controller-pairing state through the shared pairing command, without reinstalling packages.

Cleanup

exec delegates command lifetime and status; the operator restarts the Gateway and reconnects its controller.

@see src/gateway_core/pairing.py

@see src/gateway_macos/startup.sh

src/gateway_macos/reset.sh

Shell · Tier A

Reset local Gateway pairing and connection state without starting its services. Use the same account and GATEWAY_TLS_STATE_DIR as startup.sh; stop the Gateway first.

src/gateway_macos/runtime-purge.sh

Shell · Tier A

Purge local Gateway runtime data while preserving setup without starting its services. Use the same account and GATEWAY_TLS_STATE_DIR as startup.sh; stop the Gateway first.

src/gateway_macos/startup.sh

Shell · Tier B

Start the macOS Gateway using its installed platform environment.

Usage

Launch on the target macOS host after its platform installer succeeds.

Inputs

Host/port and controller host/port/scheme options override GATEWAY_* settings. Default

Side effects

Checks runtime readiness with isolated Python, then starts shared Gateway serving or outbound transport; jobs/terminals and authenticated execution belong to gateway_core.

Cleanup

Runs in the foreground; the invoking terminal/service manager owns termination. POSIX wrappers exec the Python process; Windows propagates outbound exit status.

@see src/gateway_macos/app.py

@see src/gateway_core/serve.py

@see src/gateway_core/outbound.py
